tagline: Back roads out of Little Washington, by Fodderstack and Ben Venue.
intro: Out of Washington the byway takes the back way, on Fodderstack Road and its neighbors, through the village of Flint Hill and on by Crest Hill Road to the Rappahannock River at the Fauquier line.

A second road, Ben Venue Road, runs from Flint Hill down to US 211 at Ben Venue, past a brick farmhouse built between 1844 and 1846 whose grounds keep three brick slave cabins, a kitchen and a smokehouse. Beyond it the same route carries on as Richmond Road.

moments.title: Washington
moments.text: Little Washington had 86 people in 2020 on 182 acres, and has been described as perhaps the best preserved of the county-seat towns in the Virginia Piedmont.

moments.title: Flint Hill
moments.text: A crossroads community since about 1740, the village strings out along two miles of Route 522 that were listed together as a historic district in 2012.

moments.title: Laurel Mills
moments.text: The village on the Thornton River looks much as it did when the woolen mill closed in 1927, its buildings lining one road that bends sharply at the bluff.
